t.Review gating é filtrar quem avalia seu: Review gating means filtering who reviews your business on Google. Understand why it violates the policies, how to tell if the tool you use does it and what the right way is.
t.Review gating: o erro que pode apagar to: Review gating: the mistake that can wipe out all your Google reviews
t.Um dono de restaurante me descreveu o si: A restaurant owner proudly described his system to me: a kiosk at the exit asked "how was your experience?" with a happy face and a sad face. Whoever tapped the happy one went straight to Google. Whoever tapped the sad one landed on an internal form that went to the manager's WhatsApp. "That way only good reviews go to Google", he said.
t.Esse totem tem nome técnico: review gati: That kiosk has a technical name: review gating. And what it does isn't protect the rating — it builds a rating that doesn't describe the business, in a scheme Google expressly prohibits and that can cost you the reviews you already have.
t.Pesquisa de satisfação prévia: \"de 1 a: A satisfaction survey first: "from 1 to 5, how was it?" — a 4 or 5 sees the Google button; a 1 to 3 sees a private form.
t.Totem ou tablet com carinhas: feliz leva: A kiosk or tablet with faces: happy leads to Google, sad leads to "talk to the manager".
t.E-mail ou SMS em duas etapas: primeiro \: Two-step email or SMS: first "would you recommend us?"; the Google link only appears in the second email, and only for those who said yes.
t.Link de avaliação entregue apenas a uma: A review link handed only to a list of customers hand-picked for being fans.
t.Repare que nem todo gating é software. A: Notice that not all gating is software. The most common version in Brazilian retail is human: the staff member who only hands over the review card when the customer leaves smiling. The intention is good, but the effect is the same — the business's public picture is assembled through a filter.
t.Por que o Google proíbe (e o que diz a p: Why Google prohibits it (and what the policy says)
t.As políticas de conteúdo do Google para: Google's content policies for business profiles are explicit about this: the platform does not allow selectively soliciting reviews, offering the request only to customers with a positive experience, nor discouraging negative reviews. As Google sees it, the value of reviews comes from their being an honest sample of the people who went through the business. Filtering the sample breaks exactly what makes the system worth anything.
t.O risco real: o que pode acontecer com s: The real risk: what can happen to your profile
t.Nada disso é certeza — é exposição. Você: None of this is certain — it's exposure. You're building your reputation on a practice that, if and when it's identified, wipes out exactly the asset you took years to build. It's an asymmetric risk: the gain is a decimal point on your rating, the potential loss is the whole rating.
t.O prejuízo que ninguém conta: você fica: The damage no one mentions: you go blind
t.Deixando a política de lado por um minut: Setting the policy aside for a minute, there's a silent cost that usually hurts more than the penalty.
t.Quando você desvia o cliente insatisfeit: When you divert unhappy customers to a private channel, you think you're "handling it internally". In most cases, you're just filing it away. The form lands in an inbox nobody reads, the manager's WhatsApp becomes a dumping ground for complaints, and the problem that caused the complaint keeps happening — every day, with every customer.
t.Uma crítica pública dói mais e, por doer: Public criticism hurts more and, because it hurts, it gets fixed. The repair shop that gets "I waited 3 hours past my appointment" in front of everyone changes its schedule the following week. The same shop, with gating, gets the same sentence on an internal form and keeps booking four cars for the same time slot for two more years.
t.Como saber se a ferramenta que você usa: How to tell if the tool you use practices gating
t.Muita plataforma de reputação vende gati: Many reputation platforms sell gating under a pretty name: "smart filter", "rating protection", "feedback screening", "only positive reviews go to Google". If you signed up for something like that, check these points:
t.Se descobrir que sua ferramenta faz isso: If you find out your tool does this, the fix is simple: turn off the screening and make the Google link the same for everyone. If the platform doesn't let you turn it off, it's selling you the risk as a feature — it's worth switching.
t.O jeito compatível: reduzir atrito em ve: The compliant way: reduce friction instead of filtering people
t.Então o desequilíbrio não se corrige blo: So the imbalance isn't fixed by blocking unhappy customers. It's fixed by making it easy for happy ones — who are the majority and just need a 30-second nudge. In practice:
t.Pedido compatível · ~10 segundos, pra qu: Compliant request · ~10 seconds, for any customer
t.\"Obrigado, [Nome]! Se puder, deixa sua: "Thank you, [Name]! If you can, leave your opinion on Google — just tap your phone here, it takes 30 seconds. It means a lot to us, praise or criticism."
Notice the ending: "praise or criticism". It's not ethical window dressing — it's what separates a legitimate request from gating. And in practice, almost nobody responds to that invitation by writing a complaint: someone who was unhappy would have complained on their own already.
t.\"Mas e se eu levar uma avaliação injust: "But what if I get an unfair review?"
t.Vai levar. Todo negócio leva. A defesa c: You will. Every business does. The defense against that isn't filtering — it's volume and replies.
t.Volume, porque com 200 avaliações reais: Volume, because with 200 real reviews an unfair 1-star barely moves the average; with 12 reviews, it's devastating. Replies, because an exaggerated complaint answered calmly and with facts ("we're very sorry about the wait on Saturday; we've added staff on weekends since then") convinces readers more than the complaint accuses.

t.Review gating é filtrar quem chega ao fo: Review gating is filtering who reaches the review form based on the customer's opinion — by software, kiosk or staff training. Google prohibits it, the risk is mass removal of reviews or profile suspension, and the trigger is usually a report from a customer or competitor. Along with buying reviews, it's the kind of shortcut that trades a small gain now for a big loss later. The path that works is the opposite: the same door for everyone, friction close to zero and a public reply to every complaint. That doesn't guarantee a high rating — nothing does — but it builds a reputation no one can take away from you.

h.Existe uma prática que muita ferramenta: There's a practice many reputation tools sell as a feature and Google treats as a violation: filtering who can review you. It's review gating — asking first whether the customer liked it and only sending those who said yes to Google. It seems clever, it gets results in the short term, and that's exactly why so many people fall for it. This guide explains what it is, the real risk you run, how to find out whether the tool you use does it — and how to ask for reviews in a way that doesn't put your profile in the line of fire.
h.Review gating (algo como \"portaria de a: Review gating (something like a "review gatekeeper") is any mechanism that selects who reaches the review form based on the person's opinion. The format varies, but the principle is always the same: you ask first, and the path depends on the answer.
h.Pedido verbal seletivo: a equipe é trein: Selective verbal request: staff are trained to offer the stand or QR Code only to those who gave praise.
h.O teste de uma pergunta: algum cliente s: The one-question test: is any of your customers discouraged or prevented from reaching Google because of the opinion they hold? If the answer is yes, it's gating — whether it happens through software, a kiosk or a staff member's decision.
h.Na prática, o Google trata gating no mes: In practice, Google puts gating in the same bucket as bought reviews: both produce a profile that misleads consumers. One invents customers who never existed; the other hides those who existed and didn't like it. The result on screen is the same — 4.9 stars that don't match reality.
h.E vale dizer o óbvio, já que o tema é at: And it's worth stating the obvious, since the topic is shortcuts: buying reviews is even worse and shouldn't be in any of your plans. It's fraud, Google's detectors keep getting better and removal usually comes in bulk, knocking your rating down overnight. Gating and buying are different shortcuts that come due for the same reason.
h.Vamos ser honestos sobre o tamanho do ri: Let's be honest about the size of the risk, without fearmongering. Nobody gets penalized for gating the very next minute — Google doesn't inspect kiosks in restaurants. The risk is cumulative and arrives through paths you don't control:
h.Remoção em massa das avaliações. Quando: Mass removal of reviews. When a suspicious pattern is detected — volume that only comes from the same device or link, an unrealistic rating distribution (100% five stars for months on end) — Google may remove the batch. You wake up with dozens fewer reviews and a different rating, without warning.
h.Suspensão do perfil. Em casos mais grave: Profile suspension. In more serious or repeat cases, the business profile may be suspended. Meanwhile, your business simply disappears from Maps — and recovering requires a reinstatement process, which takes time.
h.Denúncia de concorrente ou cliente. Este: Reports from competitors or customers. This is the most common trigger and the most overlooked. The customer who tapped the sad face and got diverted to the internal form notices the scheme. So do competitors who know your tool. Anyone can report the profile.
h.A ferramenta cai e leva você junto. Se a: The tool goes down and takes you with it. If the platform you hired does gating for hundreds of clients, the pattern becomes visible at its scale — and the problem splashes onto everyone who uses it.
h.Um detalhe que muita gente não sabe: per: A detail many people don't know: a profile with 100% five-star reviews converts less than a profile with 4.6 or 4.7. Brazilian consumers have learned to distrust perfection. A few 3s and 4s in the mix, with a polite reply from the owner underneath, convey more credibility than a wall of identical praise.
Walk the unhappy customer's path. This is the definitive test. Use the link, the QR or the stand as if you were a customer and answer the initial question with the worst possible rating. If you reach the Google form normally, all good. If you're diverted to an internal form, it's gating.
h.Leia a página de vendas com olho crítico: Read the sales page with a critical eye. Promises like "avoid negative reviews", "only the good ones go to Google" or "protect your rating" describe gating under another name.
h.Veja se existe uma pergunta antes do Goo: Check whether there's a question before Google. Any "how was your experience?" step before the Google link is a candidate gatekeeper. Not every survey is gating — the problem is when the answer changes the destination.
h.Olhe a distribuição das suas notas. Se s: Look at your rating distribution. If your profile has hundreds of reviews and practically none below 5 stars, something is filtering — a real business's statistics don't look like that.
h.Pergunte direto pro suporte. \"O cliente: Ask support directly. "Can a customer who gives a low rating reach Google through your system?" A written answer settles the question. Hesitation is already an answer.
h.Aqui está a virada mental que resolve o: Here's the mental shift that solves the problem. Gating tries to control who reviews. The compliant path controls how many review — offering the same open door to every customer and clearing the obstacles from the way.
h.Isso funciona por um motivo estatístico: This works for a simple statistical reason: at most decent local businesses, the typical experience is good. The problem isn't that unhappy customers review too much — it's that they're far more motivated to review than happy ones. Someone who left annoyed looks up Google on their own, in the middle of the night. Someone who left happy thinks "I'll review it later" and never does.
h.Peça pra todo cliente, sem exceção e sem: Ask every customer, without exception and without screening. The same stand, the same QR Code, the same link — for those who praised and those who complained.
h.Peça no momento certo. Logo depois da en: Ask at the right moment. Right after the service is delivered, while the customer is still on site or the experience is fresh. That's when satisfaction peaks.
h.Elimine passos. Cada toque a mais entre: Cut steps. Every extra tap between wanting to and reviewing lowers conversion. An NFC stand or QR that opens straight to the review screen beats any written instruction to "look us up on Google".
h.Nunca condicione o pedido a nota. \"Se v: Never make the request conditional on a rating. "If you give us 5 stars..." isn't just gating, it's an incentive — another violation.
Reply to all of them, especially the bad ones. A polite public reply to a complaint is worth more than the complaint not existing. Readers see an owner who cares.
h.E existe um caminho legítimo pros casos: And there's a legitimate path for cases that cross the line: reviews with insults, provably false content, spam or from people who were never customers can be reported for removal from within the business profile. It's not fast or guaranteed, but it's the right mechanism — and different from hiding genuine criticism.
